sermon.title: Believers Displeasing God (Part One)
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer shows from 1 Corinthians 10 that believers can displease God and be corrected, as Israel was even though they were under the cloud, through the sea and fed by the spiritual rock. He teaches that the rock was Christ, explains water baptism and the rivers of living water, and warns the church not to lust, practice idolatry or sexual immorality.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the title is as it appears on the video (“Belivers”); this page calls it “Believers Displeasing God.” The caption reads “vision” where the context is “division,” “316” where he appears to say “3/16,” and “Revelation 77,” which is Revelation 7:17; his “16th chapter” is kept as he said it. He reads Exodus 14:27 and the next verse together, and Mark 14:27 quotes the prophet Zechariah; both are shown. “Sinai” and “Kadesh Barnea” were spelled out where the captions were garbled. “[Unclear]” marks three spots where the captions were not clear: a word after “You” (paragraph starting at 11:19), a word after “from which we’re” (paragraph starting at 13:13), and a place name after “the church in” (paragraph starting at 14:44).

chunks.section_question: Can believers displease God and be punished for it?
chunks.short_answer: He says believers can displease God and be “disciplined for it,” and that a better word is “correction.” He lists ways God allowed Satan to correct His sinning people, including plagues, wars, famine, wild animals, family rebellion, harmful spirits and captivity, and says Christians don’t want to hear this “but it’s still Bible.”
chunks.text:
He’s going to show us that believers can displease God and be punished for it. A better word is correction. Say the word: correction. Correction. Be disciplined for it. And we find all throughout the Bible that God allowed Satan to correct God’s people that sinned through plagues, wars, acts of God, famine, wild animals, uh, family issues. David’s son died, uh, his sons rebelled, David had to deal with his own sons, uh, he caused rebellion in the home, uh, through, through Satan, uh, evil spirits, harmful spirits to individuals, and captivity. All these things can happen to, for God’s people to be corrected. But Christians don’t want to hear this, but it’s still Bible, and Paul’s going to approach this subject this morning.

And, uh, a quick, short reminder: remember, one quarter of the 16th chapter is about division, which America is full of. All of us think we got the answer, and we don’t like the other guy that has a different answer. Uh, 3/16 of his seminar is about sexual immorality, and it’s bad in America and it’s bad in the church in our day. Then he talked about idolatry, and so he took up one half of this seminar on three subjects. Then he talked about himself being an apostle and clarifying what an apostle was, and then he gave us this tremendous example of how he pursued the gospel prize using four necessities to reach it, so that he, the apostle, called to the third heaven, saw Jesus personally, would not get disqualified while he was winning others.

chunks.section_question: What did Israel experience under the cloud and through the sea? (1 Corinthians 10:1)
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul turns to the Corinthian believers and reminds them that all the fathers were under the cloud and passed through the sea. He cites Exodus 13:21 and 14:27, where God’s presence led them in a cloud and a pillar of fire and the Egyptian army was destroyed, and says today Satan is “destroyed through the death of the cross.”
chunks.text:
And with that great statement, then he turns and he points to the Corinthian believers, and he says, “Moreover, brethren, I do not want you to be unaware that all of our fathers were under the cloud and all passed through the sea.” He directing everything at them. Now in Exodus 13:21, “The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud to lead the way.” See, they were all under the cloud. The cloud spread over them, and then there was a pillar of a cloud down leading them, and so God’s presence was there in the form of a cloud. They actually saw God in the form of a cloud and a pillar of fire, and He was leading the way. All right, in Exodus 14:27, “The Lord overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea. There remained not one.” See, they all experienced the power of the enemy being destroyed.

Paul knows what he’s doing here. Are you with me so far? Then we read in Revelation 7:17 that the New Testament church, “the Lamb shall feed them and lead them into living fountains of water.” See, they were headed for Canaan land, the Promised Land, but God’s leading us to living waters. Hallelujah. I get so excited about this, and you guys look at me like, “What?” Now, not only that, but in Hebrews 2:14, “through death Jesus destroyed him that had the power of death, that is the Devil.” So see, in the sea they had the enemy of the Egyptian army, the enemy that was wanting to destroy them, destroyed. But today we have who? Satan destroyed through the death of the cross. The power of the cross, the cross is powerful. See, Satan’s destroyed. Remember, he’s rendered powerless. He don’t have power over us anymore.

chunks.text: And so Paul is explaining just like they experienced these things, we experience these things. And then he says in verse 2, 1 Corinthians 10:2, “All were baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea. All ate the same spiritual food.” Okay, every one of them. And in John 6:48, “I am the bread of life. Your fathers ate manna in the wilderness.” He said, yes, they had spiritual food, but they all died. You say, “But I’m the bread of life, you eat My food and you will never die.” Isn’t that beautiful?

chunks.short_answer: He says we identify with the death, burial and resurrection of Christ, and “something is actually done in water baptism that a lot of people don’t understand.” He says we go into the grave with Christ and come out “a new creature,” and cites Romans 6 that the body of sin might be destroyed so that we would no longer serve sin.

And in Romans 6:4 and 6 he says, “We are buried with Jesus by baptism unto death.” This is why water baptism is important. You see, we identify with the death, burial and resurrection of Christ, and something is actually done in water baptism that a lot of people don’t understand, but they need to understand it. It’s not just a little sermon or ceremony, I’m sorry, that we do in the church. He says all of us are buried with Him. When we get water baptized, we go into the grave with Christ, and as Christ was raised up out of that grave by the glory of the Father, so we should walk in newness of life. You see, He came out of the grave, but we come out of the water a new creature.

chunks.text:
Okay, he says they all drink, in verse 3, “the same spiritual drink, and they drank of that spiritual rock that followed them.” A rock followed Israel.

Wow. Now that should get your attention. I don’t remember reading no rock following anybody. Well, Paul’s going to show us. All right, Paul’s a really sharp boy, he really is. Okay, and he tells us who the rock was. That rock was Christ. Christ was following them in the wilderness. I don’t remember reading that. That’s why we need to come to church. chunks.section_question: Why did God test Israel with no water at Sinai?
chunks.short_answer: He says two and a half months after leaving Egypt God purposely brought them to a place with no water, and they failed the test and rebelled, saying they could be back in Egypt eating the leeks and onions. God then told Moses to strike the rock, and the water flowed in a stream through the camp for the people and the livestock.
chunks.text: All right, and so it happened. But let me tell you something, this was at Sinai, two and a half months after they came out of Egypt. How many months? Two and a half. And God tested them. He purposely brought them to a place where there was no water, and they failed the test. They rebelled. “You brought us out here to die in the wilderness. Man, we could be back in Egypt eating the leeks and the onions and all the cucumbers and all that stuff.” Yeah, you were slaves back there, and you were complaining there. Ain’t that right? So they failed the test and they rebelled, and then God told Moses, “Smite the rock,” and here come the water. chunks.section_question: Why did God make Israel wander 40 years, and was everyone punished?
chunks.short_answer: He says after the spies gave a bad report and the people would not go in, God punished them for disobeying and made them wander in the wilderness. Everybody who disbelieved died there, “except Joshua and Caleb, who had a different spirit,” and he says “not everybody’s punished and corrected when God does His correction.”
chunks.text: Wow. Ain’t that beautiful? But you got to remember this: after they left Mount Sinai, they traveled through this wilderness, they went to Kadesh Barnea, that second circle up there, and they sent out spies into the land. The spies came back with a bad report, they wouldn’t go in, so God punished them for disobeying Him and made them wander in the wilderness for 40 years, including the years that they came out, 40 total, to correct them. And everybody that disbelieved God died in the wilderness except Joshua and Caleb, who had a different spirit. See, in other words, not everybody’s punished and corrected when God does His correction. Hallelujah, thank God. Now, but what you got to understand, young believers, is this.

So Jesus was there with them in the wilderness before He ever became flesh and dwelt amongst us. And He was the rock, a flinty rock. It says that the water flowed out into a stream, giving water to who? 2 and a half million people. Hallelujah. Is that good? Yeah, that’s hot stuff. I like this Paul guy. Now, what does that mean for us today? John 7:38: “He that believes on Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.” You see, Jesus lives in us, so the rock is where? In us. And He says out of our bellies shall flow rivers of living water. “But this spoke He of the” what? “Spirit, which was to come.” On the day of Pentecost, the outpouring of the Holy Spirit. Americans argue about it all the time. I just can’t believe that you can argue about something so plain in the Bible and something so wonderful.

scriptures.text_nkjv: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.” But this He spoke concerning the Spirit, whom those believing in Him would receive; for the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus was not yet glorified.

chunks.section_question: Is the Holy Spirit a well of living water inside believers? (John 4:14)
chunks.short_answer: He says the Holy Ghost “had been given, but it hadn’t been given to everyone,” and now it is, and he asks why people argue about something so wonderful. He cites John 4:14 and says it is “an artesian well” that “keeps quenching your thirst” and “keeps empowering you all the time.”
chunks.text: Jesus, the rock, lives in us, and He wants to pour the waters out of us so we drink and those around us, what? Drink. Are you there? Now, He said, “But the Holy Ghost was not yet given because He was not yet glorified,” or He hadn’t died on the cross yet. And in other words, it had been given, but it hadn’t been given to everyone. Uh, Joel said the Spirit will be poured out on all flesh. It hadn’t been done that way yet, but now it’s done, and why do we want to argue about something that’s so wonderful? It just blows my mind away, because some people make a wreck of it does not mean it’s not a truth. Could that be an amen? This is a powerful truth. In John 4:14, “Whosoever drinks of the water that I will give him shall never thirst, but the water that I shall give him shall be in him,” be in, in him, and what does it do? “A well of water springing up into” what? “Everlasting life.” It’s an artesian well. It just keeps quenching your thirst, it just keeps empowering you all the time. You don’t have to wait to go to the church in [unclear] and shake. It’s there in the morning when you get up, it’s there at night when you go to bed, and it’s there between, always rising in you.

chunks.section_question: Does God approve of everything His people do? (1 Corinthians 10:5)
chunks.short_answer: He says verse 5, “with most of them God was not well pleased,” means God disapproved of their lifestyle, attitudes and decisions even though He was there and did great things for them. He says, “Just because you got God in your church, even miracles, and God is saving souls, does not mean God is pleased with everybody.”
chunks.text: Hallelujah. This is a powerful God we have, church. Powerful. And this Paul knows what he’s talking about. Now he’s setting these guys up. He said this is what God did for Israel, and they all knew that. Now, then in verse 5 he says this: “But with most of them God was not well pleased.” He disapproved of their lifestyle, He disapproved of their attitudes, He disapproved of their decisions. Yes, He was there, and He did great things for them, but that doesn’t mean He approved of what they did. Does he have the Corinthians now? Yeah. Just because you got God in your church, even miracles, and God is saving souls, does not mean God is pleased with everybody and what’s going on. Do we get that, church? Powerful, very powerful. This really helped me out as a young Christian. I can remember when God revealed it to me. It was powerful in my life. He gave me the substance to ignore sin and stick in the church and hang in there.

chunks.section_question: What are the “examples” Paul gives believers, and what is lusting after harmful things? (1 Corinthians 10:6)
chunks.short_answer: He says these things became examples “to the intent, to the purpose,” that believers should not “lust after harmful things as they lusted,” and that it applies to all believers, not just apostles. He asks whether the American church is “filled with carried-out lust.”
chunks.text: Now, “these things,” for “their bodies were scattered in the wilderness.” Verse 6: “Now these things became” what? “Examples,” a model, “to the intent that we,” us apostles and you church members, Paul says, “us” apostles. He, I’m not an apostle. “Us.” I’m Paul’s microphone, I’m just saying what he said. See, as powerful as us apostles are, these are our examples, and not just us apostles, all of you believers. It’s an example to the intent, to the purpose, that we should not, what? Lust after harmful things as they lusted. Is the American church filled with carried-out lust? Yeah.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now these things became our examples, to the intent that we should not lust after evil things as they also lusted.

chunks.section_question: Why does Paul warn the Corinthians not to become idolaters? (1 Corinthians 10:7)
chunks.short_answer: He lists problems among believers, such as drunkenness, sexual immorality, division and greed, and says Paul shows God dealt with Israel so that now “cross or no cross, he’s going to correct you.” He cites “do not become idolaters,” the people who sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and ties the golden calf party to debauchery and a “festival mentality.”
chunks.text: Are believers getting drunk? Sexual immorality. Homosexuality. Incest. Yes. Are they divided? Are they greedy? Yeah. He’s got them. He showed them God dealt with Israel, now he’s going to show them: cross or no cross, he’s going to correct you. Watch, verse 7, 1 Corinthians 10: “Do not become idolaters, as were some of them.” How many of them? Some, not everybody did it. “As it is written, the people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play.” Man, they had a big party going on, the beer, the wine, and the music playing, and they had their idol there, that golden calf, and that’s what goes along with all that debauchery: the music and the sexual immorality and, you know, the festival mentality, the big party mentality.

Then they rose early on the next day, offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

chunks.section_question: Is there a punishment for sexual immorality, and is “once saved always saved” true?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul warns, “Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and God slew 23,000 in one day,” showing there is a punishment if you don’t get it corrected. He says many preachers do American Christians a “disfavor” by teaching that through grace and faith you can do anything and are saved no matter what, and that “our God who loves us will correct us.”
chunks.text: Is America in a party mentality? Absolutely. And that’s why he talked about idolatry before sexual immorality, talked about before: “Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and God slew 23,000 in one day.” And he already showed them they were committing sexual immorality earlier. Now he’s showing them there’s a punishment for it if you don’t get it corrected. And this is the disfavor many preachers are doing to American Christians today: through grace and faith you can do anything you want, God loves you, you’re going to heaven, once saved always saved. Listen, folks, we got a God that’s not worthless. He has power, and like a parent loves their children, will discipline them, our God who loves us will correct us. Amen. He doesn’t want us destroying our life in these things. He—

faqs.question: What does he recap that Paul covered earlier in the letter?
faqs.answer: He says about a quarter of the letter was about division, 3/16 about sexual immorality, then idolatry, so one half was on three subjects. Then Paul talked about being an apostle and gave the example of how he pursued the gospel prize using four necessities so that he would not get disqualified.

faqs.question: How does he describe God’s presence with Israel in Exodus 13:21?
faqs.answer: He says the cloud spread over them and a pillar of a cloud led them, so God’s presence was there in the form of a cloud and a pillar of fire, and “He was leading the way.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so as to go by day and night.

faqs.question: What does he say the destruction of the Egyptian army illustrates?
faqs.answer: He says in the sea Israel had the enemy that wanted to destroy them destroyed, but today Satan is destroyed through the death of the cross. He says Satan is “rendered powerless” and doesn’t have power over us anymore.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Inasmuch then as the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself likewise shared in the same, that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,

faqs.question: What does he say baptism does to the old man of sin?
faqs.answer: He says “our old man of sin is crucified with Him” in water baptism, “that the body of sin might be destroyed.” He says God destroying the Egyptian army was an illustration that He was going to destroy the sinful nature in the new covenant.

scriptures.text_nkjv: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with Him, that the body of sin might be done away with, that we should no longer be slaves of sin.

faqs.question: Why does he say the water from the rock was supernatural?
faqs.answer: He says there is nothing in a stone that has anything to do with water: you can heat it or freeze it and it isn’t going to produce water. He tells younger believers, “you’re serving a supernatural God here. This is not a religion. God is a reality.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock in Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, that the people may drink.” And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.

faqs.question: How does he say Paul knew it was the same rock?
faqs.answer: He cites Deuteronomy 8:15 about the great and terrible wilderness with no water and says they wandered 38 years where there was not a drop of water. He asks, “how did they live for 38 years? The rock that followed them.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: who led you through that great and terrible wilderness, in which were fiery serpents and scorpions and thirsty land where there was no water; who brought water for you out of the flinty rock;

faqs.question: Was Jesus with Israel in the wilderness before He became flesh?
faqs.answer: He says Paul knew that rock was Jesus Christ, and so “Jesus was there with them in the wilderness before He ever became flesh and dwelt amongst us.” He says the water from the flinty rock served 2 and a half million people.

faqs.question: Do you have to wait until church to have the well of water in you?
faqs.answer: He says it keeps quenching your thirst and empowering you all the time. He says “it’s there at night when you go to bed” and it is there in the morning when you get up, always rising in you.

scriptures.text_nkjv: but whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him will never thirst. But the water that I shall give him will become in him a fountain of water springing up into everlasting life.”

faqs.question: How does he say this teaching helped him as a young Christian?
faqs.answer: He says it “really helped me out as a young Christian,” and that God revealed it to him powerfully. He says “He gave me the substance to ignore sin and stick in the church and hang in there.”

faqs.question: Are the examples in 1 Corinthians 10 only for apostles?
faqs.answer: He says Paul says “us apostles,” but it is “not just us apostles, all of you believers.” He says it is an example to the intent, to the purpose, that we should not lust after harmful things.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now these things became our examples, to the intent that we should not lust after evil things as they also lusted.

faqs.question: What does he say Israel’s party looked like in the wilderness?
faqs.answer: He says they had “a big party going on, the beer, the wine, and the music playing,” and their idol, the golden calf, and that goes along with debauchery, sexual immorality and “the big party mentality.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And do not become idolaters as were some of them. As it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.”

faqs.question: What does he mean when he says we have a God that is “not worthless”?
faqs.answer: He says “we got a God that’s not worthless. He has power, and like a parent loves their children, will discipline them,” so our God who loves us will correct us. He says God doesn’t want us destroying our life in these things.
